status: first crystallized entity dossiers; facts sourced primarily to official institutional material, project operators labeled synthesis

identity.name: Danmarks Nationalbank
identity.legal_or_institutional_form: self-governing independent institution established by law

sources.title: Board of Governors, Group Management and departments
Description of the Danish payment infrastructure (TARGET DKK)
Danes are paying more digitally – making offline payments an even more important contingency

spirit.documented_mission: Stable prices, safe payments and a stable financial system; the statutory object is to maintain a safe and secure monetary system and facilitate/regulate money circulation and credit.
spirit.legitimacy_basis: Danmarks Nationalbank Act of 1936, institutional independence, and public monetary mandate.
spirit.project_interpretation: Spirit is the public mandate and trust claim: money and payments should remain reliable enough for society to coordinate.

mind.governance: Three-member Board of Governors has overall management; the Board of Governors has sole responsibility for shaping and adjusting monetary policy. Group Management combines the Board with heads of seven departments for priorities, strategy and policy.
mind.decision_system: Monetary policy under Denmark's fixed-exchange-rate framework; continuous analysis of inflation, financial stability and payments.
mind.knowledge_system: Economic/financial analysis, statistics, market operations and oversight of financial infrastructure.
mind.feedback_and_oversight: Formal governance structure provides political insight while preserving monetary-policy independence; infrastructure oversight uses international standards.

body.people_or_members: Institutional staff and three-governor top management; detailed current headcount not asserted in this dossier.
body.money_or_budget: 2025 profit DKK 24.7 billion; gold price gains contributed DKK 18.5 billion to portfolio returns.
body.infrastructure: Central-bank financial portfolios, settlement/payment functions, banknotes/coins and oversight of central payment/securities systems.
body.operational_capacity: In 2025, systems in the Danish payments infrastructure carried DKK 838 billion on an average banking day.

history.event: Established to restore monetary order after the 1813 state bankruptcy.
Current Nationalbank Act reorganized the institution and codified its mandate/governance.
Denmark's modern fixed exchange rate policy dates from this period.

relationships.target: monetary policy and central-bank functions in Denmark
Danish central government on selected debt/borrowing tasks
Danish central government after allocations under the Act

operators.why: Payments are observable financial flows through infrastructure.
operators.test: Map sources, settlement systems, throughput, bottlenecks and outage/counterparty risks.
operators.fails_if: Used as a metaphor without actual flow data.

operators.why: Infrastructure oversight and financial-stability analysis are observation/assessment functions.
operators.test: Trace what is monitored, standards used, recommendations issued and what remains outside the observation frame.

operators.why: Settlement, access and monetary-policy mechanisms change what financial actors can transmit or price.
operators.fails_if: No state or capability transition can be specified.

operators.why: Mission is justified by stable prices, safe payments and systemic stability rather than institutional activity itself.
operators.test: Use outcome indicators plus failure/externality measures, not institutional output alone.
operators.fails_if: Profit or publication volume substitutes for mandate outcomes.

measurable_current_examples: DKK 838 billion average banking-day payment throughput in 2025
fruit.measurement_limits: Counterfactual stability is difficult to observe directly: absence of failure does not prove a specific intervention caused stability.

known_unknowns: Counterfactual contribution of individual oversight actions to crises that did not occur.
Full causal allocation between central-bank actions and broader market/EU/global conditions.
shadow.missingness_mechanism: Some desired outcomes are prevention outcomes and therefore structurally hard to observe; causal attribution is incomplete rather than secret.
shadow.evidence_gap: A deeper dossier needs longitudinal indicators for inflation, exchange-rate stability, system incidents, liquidity and recommendation follow-through.

tensions.text: How does an independent monetary authority maintain public legitimacy while preserving insulation from day-to-day political control?
How should safe-payment performance be judged when the highest-value outcome is often the non-occurrence of disruption?

discovery_questions: Can the House distinguish operational throughput (River) from trust/legitimacy (Spirit) and oversight quality (Eye) without collapsing them into one stability score?
Where are the most important single points of failure or alternative routes in Danish payment infrastructure?
Which Nationalbank recommendations measurably change capability or risk in the institutions receiving them?
dossiers.evidence_boundary: No claim here rates Danish monetary policy or political choices. Project-operator mappings are analytical syntheses over official institutional facts.

scale_profile.operating_scale: National central bank embedded in European and global settlement networks.
constituent_layers: three-member Board of Governors and departments
Danish financial institutions and connected clearing/payment systems
key_dependencies: Eurosystem TARGET Services for central DKK settlement
participating financial institutions and clearing systems
international standards and cooperative oversight for cross-border infrastructure
scale_profile.scope_boundary: Danmarks Nationalbank oversees important payment instruments and systems but does not thereby supervise every individual company in the payments ecosystem.

reproduction_mechanisms: statutory mandate and governance under the Nationalbank Act
specialist central-bank staff and operating procedures
monetary-policy and settlement rules
international financial-market-infrastructure standards
recurring analysis, oversight and reporting
reproduction_and_correction.succession_or_training: Institutional roles, departments, documented rules and professional expertise allow monetary, settlement and oversight functions to continue through personnel turnover.
correction_channels: public analysis of incidents and resilience
reproduction_and_correction.exit_or_appeal: Access to individual payment/settlement systems is governed by explicit participation rules; oversight findings and public-law accountability are distinct from ordinary consumer choice or political control.
reproduction_and_correction.observed_change: Settlement of Danish kroner moved from Kronos2 to TARGET Services at Easter 2025; after payment disruptions in July 2025 and May 2026, sector contingency work expanded offline card capability for basic purchases.

visibility_and_access.public_observability: Mandate, governance, annual accounts, monetary-policy analysis, infrastructure descriptions and annual oversight conclusions are publicly documented.
visibility_and_access.restricted_or_confidential: Detailed security, cyber-resilience, operational incident and participant-sensitive information is not necessarily public in full.
visibility_and_access.structural_missingness: Prevention and resilience outcomes are partly counterfactual: a failure that did not occur is difficult to attribute to one control or institution.
visibility_and_access.status_guard: Restricted operational information or central-bank independence is not evidence of wrongdoing; secrecy, confidentiality and legal authority remain separate questions.

longitudinal_indicators.unit: DKK billion per average banking day
longitudinal_indicators.reading: The value moving through core Danish payment infrastructure increased materially year over year.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Throughput is scale/load, not a standalone measure of safety, social value or policy quality.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: Reported annual profit rose, with gold price gains a major contributor in 2025.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Central-bank profit is market-sensitive and must not substitute for mandate outcomes such as price, payment or financial stability.

identity.name: Wikimedia Foundation
identity.jurisdiction_or_scope: Global movement support; U.S.-based nonprofit operating globally

sources.title: Requests for content alteration and takedown, Jul–Dec 2025

spirit.documented_mission: Enable people around the world to collect and develop educational content under free licenses or in the public domain and disseminate it effectively and globally; protect and sustain free knowledge projects.
spirit.legitimacy_basis: Nonprofit mission plus volunteer/community governance traditions and public commitment to free knowledge.
spirit.project_interpretation: Spirit is the claim that knowledge should remain freely shareable and available across generations.

mind.governance: Board oversees management/strategy; a mix of community- and affiliate-selected and Board-selected trustees plus founder seat is described in the 2026 trustee materials.
mind.decision_system: Foundation executive/board planning plus decentralized volunteer editorial communities; these are related but not identical governance systems.
mind.knowledge_system: Volunteer editing, moderation, software/data systems, research/analytics, transparency reporting and movement planning.
mind.feedback_and_oversight: Annual plans, community consultation, transparency reports, audits, Board oversight and public project histories.

body.people_or_members: About 650 staff in 46 countries according to 2026 trustee materials, alongside a much larger global volunteer movement.
body.money_or_budget: FY2026–27 annual budget USD 240.0 million: 48% technology, 29% volunteer support, 12% fundraising, 11% general/administrative.
body.infrastructure: Servers/platform infrastructure, APIs, software, data systems, fundraising, legal support and safety/trust systems supporting Wikipedia and sister projects.
body.operational_capacity: Wikipedia hosts over 65 million volunteer-authored articles in 300+ languages and receives over 15 billion visits monthly according to 2026 trustee materials.

history.event: Wikimedia Foundation established to support Wikimedia projects.
Annual planning explicitly focused on changing information consumption, regulation, misinformation/disinformation and platform conditions.
Budget increases technology investment amid AI/bot scraping, infrastructure and audience/contributor challenges.

relationships.target: applicable legal regimes including EU Digital Services Act for Wikipedia as VLOP

operators.why: A centralized nonprofit materially hosts a decentralized knowledge movement with differentiated internal roles.
operators.test: Map which functions are Foundation-owned versus volunteer/community-owned.
operators.fails_if: Foundation and volunteer communities are treated as one institution.

operators.why: Legal takedown/user-data requests, account permissions and editorial/community processes are distinct access/transition gates.
operators.test: Specify which body controls each gate and what can be appealed.
operators.fails_if: All content moderation is attributed to the Foundation.

operators.why: Transparency reports, community review and public histories expose decision/evidence processes.
operators.test: Measure what requests/decisions are visible and what categories remain opaque.
operators.fails_if: Transparency reporting is mistaken for full observability.

operators.why: The movement's mission depends on growing independent volunteer contribution and reusable free knowledge.
operators.test: Does Foundation support increase contributor/community capability rather than central dependency?
operators.fails_if: Outputs grow while volunteer capability or community autonomy erodes.

fruit.measurement_limits: Traffic and article count are incomplete proxies for knowledge quality, contributor health, representation, trust and public value.

known_unknowns: How AI-mediated consumption changes attribution, volunteer incentives and direct readership over time.
How well headline scale metrics capture representation and contributor health.
shadow.missingness_mechanism: Some platform/community health dimensions are difficult to summarize in a single centralized dataset because authority and activity are distributed.
shadow.evidence_gap: A deeper longitudinal dossier should combine editor retention, language coverage, governance participation, legal pressure, reader behavior and infrastructure load.

tensions.text: The Foundation is centralized as an infrastructure/funding/legal organization while the movement and editorial production are unusually decentralized.
How much central investment can increase resilience without displacing community capability or governance legitimacy?
How should Wikipedia optimize for reach in an AI/scraping environment without turning attention metrics into the end itself?

discovery_questions: Can Garden be operationalized as volunteer capability growth rather than content volume?
Which Doors are community-controlled, Foundation-controlled, state/legal, or technical—and where do these overlap?
Does increased API/AI infrastructure spending preserve the mission of free knowledge while changing the relationship between readers, contributors and external platforms?
dossiers.evidence_boundary: This dossier does not rate Wikimedia political content or editorial viewpoints. It distinguishes Foundation governance from volunteer editorial governance.

scale_profile.operating_scale: A U.S.-based nonprofit infrastructure organization supporting a global, decentralized volunteer knowledge movement.
constituent_layers: readers, donors, developers and content reusers
key_dependencies: search/referral ecosystems and increasingly API/bot/AI reuse channels
scale_profile.scope_boundary: The Wikimedia Foundation is not identical with Wikipedia's volunteer editorial communities and does not centrally make ordinary article-content decisions.

reproduction_mechanisms: free licenses that permit reuse and continuation
MediaWiki software and shared technical infrastructure
volunteer onboarding, editing norms and community governance
affiliate/grant support
Board and staff succession
documentation, archives and public policies
reproduction_and_correction.succession_or_training: New contributors learn through editing interfaces, help systems, mentoring/community norms and role progression; organizational staff and trustees change while the mission and platform persist.
reproduction_and_correction.exit_or_appeal: Volunteer participation is non-employment and can cease; community sanctions and content decisions have project-specific review processes; freely licensed content can be reused outside Foundation-operated sites subject to license terms.
reproduction_and_correction.observed_change: The FY2026–27 plan increases investment in technology and volunteer support while explicitly responding to declining referral traffic, bot/scraping load and the need to convert readers into repeat readers, contributors and donors.

visibility_and_access.public_observability: Articles, edit histories, many governance discussions, policies, annual plans, budgets, audits and transparency reports are publicly accessible.
visibility_and_access.restricted_or_confidential: User data, safety investigations, security controls, personnel matters and some legal requests cannot be fully public; transparency reports aggregate parts of this activity.
visibility_and_access.structural_missingness: Authority is distributed across hundreds of communities and projects, so contributor health, representation and governance quality cannot be inferred from one Foundation dashboard.
visibility_and_access.status_guard: A private user-data process or non-public safety response is not evidence of editorial manipulation; Foundation corporate authority and community editorial authority must remain distinct.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: The planned annual budget increases while the Foundation invests in platform and movement resilience.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Budget growth does not by itself show knowledge quality, contributor health or public value.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: Technology remains the largest budget category and rises amid bot/scraping and product/infrastructure pressures.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Spending is an input; resilience and mission outcomes require separate measures.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: Direct support for volunteers and the movement increases in the plan.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Funding allocated to support is not equivalent to contributor retention, autonomy or satisfaction.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: The annual report describes more than 66 million Wikipedia articles across 300+ languages.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Article count is a stock measure and not a quality, representation or readership measure.

identity.name: CERN
identity.jurisdiction_or_scope: European organization with global scientific participation
identity.legal_or_institutional_form: intergovernmental organization governed by Member States

sources.title: CERN publishes its strategy and main objectives for 2026–2030
2026 European Strategy for Particle Physics update
CERN publishes its strategy and main objectives for the period 2026–2030
25 by ’25 initiative: diversity progress at CERN
2024 Annual Report – Chapter VI of the Staff Rules and Regulations

spirit.documented_mission: Discovery through science, technological innovation, bringing nations together, inspiration and education; pursue fundamental understanding while serving a broad scientific community.
spirit.legitimacy_basis: Intergovernmental convention, Member State governance, scientific peer communities and long-running shared infrastructure.
spirit.project_interpretation: Spirit is long-horizon shared inquiry: nations sustain infrastructure that no single ordinary laboratory could reproduce alone.

mind.governance: CERN Council is highest authority and approves programmes/budgets; Scientific Policy Committee and Finance Committee assist; Director-General manages the laboratory.
mind.decision_system: Scientific strategy, Council decisions, programme prioritization, experiment collaborations and technical programme management.
mind.knowledge_system: Experimental particle physics, accelerator science, theory, computing, engineering, open scientific collaboration and external institutes.
mind.feedback_and_oversight: Council governance, scientific committees, international strategy process and experiment/scientific review.

body.people_or_members: 25 Member States and 11 Associated Member States; over 600 institutes/universities worldwide use CERN facilities.
body.money_or_budget: Member States contribute to capital and operating costs; experiments also receive substantial financing/construction support from participating funding agencies outside CERN's direct budget.
body.infrastructure: Accelerator complex including LHC/HL-LHC programme, detectors, computing, laboratories, civil engineering and support infrastructure.
body.operational_capacity: 2026–2030 top priority is timely completion of HL-LHC and detector upgrades; long-term objective is to be ready to seek Council approval for FCC-ee in 2028.

history.event: Convention entered into force, establishing CERN.
Higgs boson discovery at the LHC.
Updated European Strategy and CERN 2026–2030 strategy set current medium/long-term priorities.

relationships.target: national and international experiment funding agencies

operators.why: Large-scale shared research infrastructure contains differentiated experiments, departments and external collaborations.
operators.test: Map local experiment autonomy versus shared infrastructure/governance.
operators.fails_if: CERN is treated as one homogeneous scientific actor.

operators.why: Long-horizon engineering and experimentation transform money, expertise and hardware into capability and knowledge.
operators.test: Track inputs, milestones, technical learning, failed paths and resulting capability.
operators.fails_if: Only successful discoveries are counted and engineering learning is ignored.

operators.why: Training, shared facilities and international collaboration can grow future scientific/engineering capability.
operators.test: Measure transferable training, institute participation and technology/knowledge spillovers.
operators.fails_if: The system produces outputs without expanding participant capability.

operators.why: Membership, experiment participation, facility access and strategic approval are distinct access gates.
operators.test: Specify governance/technical conditions for each form of access.
operators.fails_if: Scientific openness is assumed to imply equal institutional access.

fruit.measurement_limits: Discovery value is uncertain ex ante; narrow near-term return metrics can miss long-horizon scientific option value and capability spillovers.

known_unknowns: Future scientific payoff and total long-term opportunity cost of next-generation collider choices.
Distribution of scientific/industrial return across Member and non-Member participants.
shadow.missingness_mechanism: Long-horizon research contains irreducible uncertainty; future discoveries cannot be directly observed before investment decisions.
shadow.evidence_gap: A deeper dossier needs programme costs, schedule risk, environmental impacts, procurement/industrial return and training outcomes in comparable time series.

tensions.text: CERN must balance fundamental scientific priorities, stakeholder value, long-lived infrastructure and future-option decisions over decades.
How should institutions evaluate projects whose central value is discovering what cannot be predicted in advance?
How does a shared intergovernmental House preserve scientific exploration while satisfying financial and political accountability?

discovery_questions: Can Fruit evaluation represent option value and capability creation without reducing science to near-term deliverables?
Which parts of CERN are modular enough to innovate locally, and which shared systems are single points of failure?
How do Member-State contributions, experimental funding and industrial return shape the actual network of capability?
dossiers.evidence_boundary: No assessment here ranks collider projects or makes political recommendations. Operator mappings are project syntheses.

scale_profile.operating_scale: Intergovernmental research organization operating shared accelerator infrastructure for a global scientific network.
constituent_layers: CERN management and roughly institution-scale staff functions
600+ participating institutes/universities and wider user communities
key_dependencies: accelerator, detector, computing and energy infrastructure
scale_profile.scope_boundary: CERN owns and operates major laboratory infrastructure but experiment collaborations and their external funding are not simply identical with CERN's central organization.

reproduction_mechanisms: international convention and Council governance
training of scientists, engineers and technicians
technical documentation and operational practice
long-lived experiment collaborations
member/institute networks
open scientific publication and knowledge transfer
reproduction_and_correction.succession_or_training: Early-career researchers, students, fellows and technical staff learn within shared facilities and collaborations while institutions continually send new cohorts.
correction_channels: scientific peer review and experimental replication
reproduction_and_correction.exit_or_appeal: Personnel have formal dispute-resolution procedures; scientific priorities are revisited through CERN Council and the European Strategy process rather than being fixed permanently by one leadership cohort.
reproduction_and_correction.observed_change: Slovenia joined as a Member State in 2025, bringing the current total to 25; the 2026–2030 strategy makes timely HL-LHC completion the top five-year priority and sets a 2028 Council decision horizon for seeking approval of the FCC-ee project.

visibility_and_access.public_observability: Mission, Member States, governance, strategy, scientific results, annual reports and substantial technical/scientific documentation are public.
visibility_and_access.restricted_or_confidential: Personnel cases, security-sensitive infrastructure details, procurement negotiations and some operational data are legitimately restricted.
visibility_and_access.structural_missingness: Scientific option value and future discoveries are unknowable ex ante; collaboration costs and benefits are distributed across CERN and external institutes/funding agencies.
visibility_and_access.status_guard: Restricted technical/personnel information is not evidence against scientific validity; scientific claims are judged by data, methods and review, not by organizational openness alone.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: CERN reported 2024 as the best proton-proton production year to that point, with raw-data collection more than doubling the cited 2023 amount.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Raw data volume measures operational/scientific throughput, not discovery quality or efficiency by itself.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: The reported share of women among staff, fellows and graduates increased over the initiative period.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: This indicator covers one diversity dimension and one defined personnel population; it is not a complete measure of inclusion or national representation.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: Slovenia's 2025 accession expanded CERN to 25 Member States.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Membership count does not capture the scale of non-member cooperation or scientific participation.

identity.name: International Committee of the Red Cross
identity.jurisdiction_or_scope: Operations in armed conflict and other situations of violence worldwide
identity.legal_or_institutional_form: private association under Swiss law with international humanitarian mandate/status

sources.title: The governing bodies of the ICRC

spirit.documented_mission: Protect lives and dignity of people affected by armed conflict and other violence, assist them, and promote respect for international humanitarian law.
spirit.legitimacy_basis: Humanitarian mandate, Geneva Conventions context, neutrality/independence/impartiality principles and long-standing field practice.
spirit.project_interpretation: Spirit is the legitimacy required to enter conflict environments where ordinary political alignment could destroy access.

mind.governance: Assembly is supreme governing body; Assembly Council supports it; Directorate is executive body responsible for day-to-day operational effectiveness.
mind.decision_system: Field assessment, confidential dialogue/negotiation, protection work, legal interpretation, humanitarian programming and operational prioritization.
mind.knowledge_system: Field presence, legal expertise, tracing/protection data, health/water assessments and programme monitoring/evaluation.
mind.feedback_and_oversight: Annual reporting, evaluation, accountability-to-affected-people processes, policies and donor reporting.

body.people_or_members: Operations in more than 90 countries; institutional workforce and Red Cross/Red Crescent partnerships not reduced to one headcount in this dossier.
body.money_or_budget: Around CHF 1.76 billion in contributions sustained 2025 operations; 84% came from governments and the European Commission, and 45% of funding was flexible.
body.infrastructure: Field offices, logistics, medical support, water/sanitation projects, detention visits, tracing systems and humanitarian supply capacity.
body.operational_capacity: 2025 examples include improved water/shelter/sanitary access for 33.53 million people, 8.47 million primary-care consultations at supported centres, and 28,693 people's fate/whereabouts clarified.

history.event: Worked amid more than 130 armed conflicts according to 2025 annual reporting.

relationships.target: states, European Commission, Red Cross/Red Crescent societies and other public/private sources
states and armed actors in conflict settings
people affected by armed conflict and other violence

operators.why: Humanitarian access to detainees, communities and conflict areas depends on negotiated permission, neutrality and trust.
operators.test: Map who controls access, what conditions apply, and where access is denied or partial.
operators.fails_if: Access is described without identifying controlling actors and constraints.

operators.why: The ICRC often operates between conflict parties and affected people without becoming a belligerent.
operators.test: Assess whether intermediary positioning creates practical access while preserving independence.
operators.fails_if: Neutrality is assumed from mission language without examining operational relationships.

operators.why: Many interventions aim not only at relief but resilience/capability such as water, health and rehabilitation.
operators.test: Measure whether assistance restores independent functioning and local capacity.
operators.fails_if: Immediate output is mistaken for durable capability.

operators.why: Conflict conditions create systematic missingness: inaccessible areas, missing persons, confidentiality and security constraints.
operators.test: Record why populations/events are unobserved and how conclusions change under access limitations.
operators.fails_if: Unknown conflict information is treated as concealed misconduct by default.

fruit.measurement_limits: Humanitarian outputs do not by themselves identify counterfactual lives saved, durable resilience, or effects where access is denied.

known_unknowns: Needs and harms in places without sufficient humanitarian access.
Counterfactual effects of confidential dialogue and prevention work.
Long-run dependence/capability effects of emergency assistance in repeated crises.
shadow.missingness_mechanism: Conflict access, security, confidentiality and disrupted records can make missingness non-random.
shadow.evidence_gap: A deeper dossier should compare access constraints, flexible versus earmarked funding, repeated-country exposure and local-capacity outcomes over time.

tensions.text: A large share of ICRC funding comes from governments/European Commission while the organization emphasizes independence and neutrality.
How does funding concentration interact with perceived and operational independence?
When should emergency relief prioritize direct delivery versus local capability-building under severe time and security constraints?

discovery_questions: Can Door analysis quantify humanitarian access rather than treating neutrality as an abstract principle?
Does flexible funding improve the organization's ability to follow need rather than donor earmarks?
Where does repeated emergency assistance become capability-building, and where can it unintentionally create dependency?
dossiers.evidence_boundary: Funding composition is a documented fact, not evidence of compromised neutrality. Any causal claim about donor influence requires separate evidence.

scale_profile.operating_scale: Independent humanitarian organization operating globally through delegations, missions and partnerships in armed-conflict settings.
constituent_layers: states and armed actors whose cooperation affects access
key_dependencies: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement cooperation
scale_profile.scope_boundary: The ICRC is one component of the wider Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement and does not control states, armed groups, National Societies or the humanitarian system as a whole.

reproduction_mechanisms: mandate grounded in the Geneva Conventions and Movement statutes
delegation practice, professional training and operational doctrine
institutional memory and annual reporting
partnerships within the Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement
recurring donor appeals and logistics systems
reproduction_and_correction.succession_or_training: Field and headquarters roles are reproduced through professional recruitment, training, delegation practice and documented humanitarian/protection methods rather than personal continuity with founders.
correction_channels: programme adaptation to access and need
reproduction_and_correction.exit_or_appeal: Affected people do not 'join' the ICRC, so membership exit is not the relevant test; meaningful feedback, complaint/accountability routes and the ability to adapt or discontinue programmes are more appropriate correction measures.
reproduction_and_correction.observed_change: From 2024 to 2025 reported donor contributions fell while the share of flexible funding rose; operational outputs moved differently by category, showing why one aggregate success score would be misleading.

visibility_and_access.public_observability: Annual operational/financial reporting, many programme figures, policies and evaluation/accountability material are public.
visibility_and_access.restricted_or_confidential: Protection dialogue with conflict parties, sensitive individual cases, security information and personal data are often confidential by design.
visibility_and_access.structural_missingness: Access restrictions, conflict insecurity, disrupted records and confidentiality make missingness non-random; the hardest-hit places may be the hardest to measure.
visibility_and_access.status_guard: Confidential humanitarian dialogue is a working method and not evidence of hidden allegiance; confidentiality and neutrality must not be collapsed into secrecy-as-guilt.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: Reported contributions declined between the two annual reports.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Contribution totals are financing inputs and do not alone measure unmet need, efficiency or humanitarian impact.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: The flexible share rose, increasing the portion that can be allocated where needs emerge rather than only to earmarked purposes.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Flexibility does not by itself establish better outcomes; allocation quality and access still matter.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: The reported number nearly doubled year over year.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: Case mix, conflict context, backlog and data availability may differ; this is not a controlled productivity comparison.
The number depends on conflict patterns, tracing caseload and feasible access, not solely organizational performance.

longitudinal_indicators.reading: Reported reach remained of similar order while falling modestly.
longitudinal_indicators.limit: The 2024 and 2025 wording/categories are not perfectly identical, so the comparison should be treated as approximate.
